scope: Public official sources only; no account, DNS, SSH, token, or server inspection. Source summaries, not a legal interpretation.

release.note: Latest was checked for this dated finding only. The helper never resolves latest or selects a digest automatically.

findings.fact: Tunnel is available on all plans. This is connector availability, not unrestricted permission to transfer public large audio files.
Publishing an application does not require a paid Cloudflare Access plan. Access policies are a separate authentication feature.

findings.section: Prerequisites; Create a tunnel; Connect an application
findings.fact: Publishing requires a domain on Cloudflare. Remotely managed tunnels use config_src=cloudflare; their ingress configuration is stored remotely.
Full setup uses Cloudflare authoritative nameservers and is available on Free, Pro, Business, and Enterprise.
Keeping external authoritative DNS while proxying selected hostnames via partial setup requires Business or Enterprise; it is unavailable on Free/Pro.

findings.section: How can Tunnel be used with Partial DNS (CNAME Setup)?; Large-file and streaming traffic through Tunnel
findings.fact: Tunnel can use full or partial DNS setup. Public hostname routes use the reverse proxy and carry the large-file restriction; private routes are distinct.
For Free, Pro, and Business public hostname routes, Cloudflare explicitly requires an appropriate specific paid service to serve video and other large files.

findings.section: Content Delivery Network (Free, Pro, or Business)
findings.fact: The CDN section requires specific paid services for non-Enterprise large-file/video serving and reserves the ability to limit or disable disproportionate audio, picture, or other large-file use without those services. No public audio eligibility or numeric safe threshold is established here.

--token-file PATH is for remotely managed tunnels only and requires cloudflared 2025.4.0 or newer. --no-autoupdate prevents updater drift; metrics can bind explicitly to loopback. Debug logs can disclose request headers, so the unit uses info.

findings.section: Credentials / LoadCredential=; Environment variables / %d credential directory example
findings.fact: LoadCredential reads a protected source into the service credential directory. The service references a file path with %d rather than embedding secret contents in ExecStart or Environment. Requires systemd credential support (247+).

findings.section: 2. Review your DNS records / Common records
findings.fact: Quick scan is not guaranteed to discover all DNS records. Review the complete provider zone, including existing website and email records, before switching authoritative nameservers.

findings.section: Disable DNSSEC; Migrate to Cloudflare with DNSSEC active
findings.fact: Changing nameservers while the old DS remains cached can cause validating resolvers to return SERVFAIL. The documented non-multisigner path removes the old DS and waits for its TTL before changing nameservers, then restores DNSSEC with the new DS after migration.

operator_constraints: Parent reports a new account, Squarespace authoritative DNS, an existing DS, and Google mail MX records; those account/domain facts were not independently inspected by this task.

Before any parent-run migration: audit/export all DNS records, preserve Google MX plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC and verification records, review DNSSEC/DS TTL handling, and record rollback. Do not alter apex/www proxy behavior as part of this connector work.

Public connector examples are control-plane-only. Audio uploads/downloads require R2 or another approved transfer architecture. R2 activation, billing, eligibility, free allowances, and integration remain with the parent; this task makes no free-audio-service promise.
Chunking, changing cache settings, or splitting files does not establish permission under the cited terms. Do not broaden ingress as a workaround.
Keep the local private engine/interface intact and MCP private. cloudflared is a network connector, not an MCP server.
